title: Nexus skill declaration
description: Schema for *.skill.json files consumed by codegen/generate.py. Each file declares one skill — a named bucket of tools that activate together via the Skill tool. Tools self-link to a skill via the per-tool *.tool.json `skill` field (see tool_schema.json); this file only carries skill-level metadata + activation behavior + the long-form instructions the model sees on activation. Skill membership is therefore derived (no second source-of-truth list to drift).

$schema.description: Editor hint pointing at this file. Allows VS Code / similar editors to validate the document on save.

name.description: Skill identifier. snake_case. Must match the filename (without .skill.json) and the value of the `skill` field on every tool that belongs to this bucket.

description.description: One-line skill description. Surfaced on the Skill tool's manifest entry so the model can decide whether activating this skill is relevant. Keep concise — long-form prose belongs in `instructions`.

instructions.description: Long-form, markdown-friendly instructions injected as the Skill tool's tool_result when the model invokes Skill('<name>'). This is where 'how to use these tools well' guidance lives — workflow patterns, recommended sequences, common pitfalls. The system prompt's per-tool blurbs handle the catalog-level descriptions; instructions[] handles the playbook-level guidance. Optional: omit (or set to empty string) for skills that are just a bucket of tools with no extra workflow notes.

default.description: Initial activation state on session start. 'always_on' skills are unconditionally active — their tools appear in tools[] from turn 1. 'deferred' skills require an explicit Skill('<name>') call to activate; until then their tools are omitted from tools[] entirely (uniform across all providers — see plan giggly-watching-pie.md for why we don't use Anthropic's defer_loading beta flag). Most product-specific skills should be 'deferred' so the cold-start tool list stays small; 'always_on' is reserved for the always-relevant skill (typically there's only one).
